group.title: Work and study basics
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A list of times when things will happen.
examples: My {schedule} is full on Monday.
wrong: I eat my schedule for lunch.
The schedule are on the wall.

words.meaning: An event where people come together to talk about work.
examples: We have a {meeting} at ten o’clock.
wrong: I wore my meeting on my feet.
She meetings with her manager.

words.meaning: A person you work with.
examples: My {colleague} helped me with the spreadsheet.
wrong: A colleague is a person you have never heard of and never work with.
He colleagues a long report.

words.meaning: A person who is in charge of a team or a place.
examples: The {manager} thanked us for our hard work.
wrong: The manager is a person who never decides anything and works for no one.
She managers the team.

words.meaning: A planned time to meet someone.
examples: I have a dentist {appointment} at four.
wrong: I met a stranger on the street by appointment, but we never planned it.
She appointment the doctor.

words.meaning: A person who buys goods or services.
examples: The {customer} asked for a refund.
wrong: The customer sells the goods to the shop.
He customers many things.

words.meaning: A document that gives information about something.
examples: She wrote a short {report} on sales.
wrong: I ate a report for breakfast.
He reports are on his desk.

words.meaning: A group of people who work together.
examples: Our {team} meets every Monday.
wrong: I am the only person in our team of twelve.
He teams in the sales department.

words.meaning: A place where people do desk work.
examples: I take the bus to the {office}.
wrong: I cook dinner in the office of my pocket.
She office at nine.

words.meaning: To ask for goods or food to be brought to you.
examples: We will {order} pizza for lunch.
wrong: I order a pizza, so I make it myself.
She orders me about food.

words.meaning: The person in charge of other workers.
examples: My {boss} asked me to finish the report.
wrong: A boss is a person who works for nobody and has no job.

words.meaning: A period of time when someone teaches something.
examples: We have an English {lesson} at ten.
wrong: A lesson is a long vacation from school.

words.meaning: A formal test of what you know.
examples: She studied all night for the {exam}.
wrong: An exam is a party at the end of the day.

words.meaning: Work that a teacher gives students to do at home.
examples: I do my {homework} after dinner.
wrong: Homework is the work that teachers do at school.

words.meaning: An area of study, such as history.
examples: Math is my favorite {subject}.
wrong: A subject is a type of vegetable.

words.meaning: A system of words that people use to speak and write.
examples: Spanish is a beautiful {language}.
wrong: A language is a part of the body that you use to walk.

words.meaning: A book with empty pages for writing notes.
examples: She wrote the words in her {notebook}.
wrong: A notebook is a small machine that cooks food.

words.meaning: A book that gives the meanings of words.
examples: I looked up the word in the {dictionary}.
wrong: A dictionary is a book of maps.

words.meaning: A small computer that you can carry.
examples: He works on his {laptop} at the café.
wrong: A laptop is a large machine that stays in a factory.

words.meaning: A machine that puts words or pictures on paper.
examples: The {printer} is out of paper.
wrong: A printer is a machine that cuts bread.

words.meaning: A message that you send on a computer.
examples: I sent her an {email} this morning.
wrong: An email is a letter that a postman brings to your door in a box.

words.meaning: A piece of information that you send or leave for someone.
examples: I left you a {message} on your phone.
wrong: A message is a kind of fruit.

words.meaning: To telephone someone.
examples: I will {call} you tonight.
wrong: I call my friend by sending her a letter.

words.meaning: A secret word that lets you use a computer or account.
examples: Do not tell anyone your {password}.
wrong: A password is a word that everyone shares on a public sign.

words.meaning: A place on the internet with information about something.
examples: The shop has a good {website}.
wrong: A website is a building made of bricks.

words.meaning: To copy a file from the internet to your computer.
examples: You can {download} the game for free.
wrong: I download a file by deleting it.

words.meaning: Connected to the internet.
examples: The {online} shop delivers quickly.
wrong: The shop is online, so we must walk to it on the street.

words.meaning: The flat part of a computer or phone where you see pictures.
examples: The {screen} of my phone is broken.
wrong: A screen is the part of a computer that you type on.

words.meaning: The set of keys you press to type.
examples: She typed the letter on the {keyboard}.
wrong: A keyboard is a screen that shows pictures.

words.meaning: A small object that stores power for a phone or a toy.
examples: My phone {battery} is almost empty.
wrong: A battery is a kind of food that you eat hot.

words.meaning: A device that fills a battery with power.
examples: I forgot my phone {charger} at home.
wrong: A charger is a thing that you wear on your head.

words.meaning: The worldwide system that connects computers.
examples: I read the news on the {internet}.
wrong: The internet is a book that you borrow at a library.

words.meaning: A picture taken with a camera.
examples: She took a {photo} of the sunset.
wrong: A photo is a sound you hear in a quiet room.

words.meaning: A recording of moving pictures.
examples: We watched a funny {video} online.
wrong: A video is a still picture that does not move.

words.meaning: A paper or file with written information.
examples: Please sign this {document} and send it back.
wrong: A document is a machine that prints in color.

words.meaning: A holder for papers or files on a desk or computer.
examples: Put the file in the blue {folder}.
wrong: A folder is a tool for cutting paper.

words.meaning: To make something that is exactly like another thing.
examples: Please {copy} the file onto this disk.
wrong: I copy a page by writing something new.

words.meaning: To produce words or pictures on paper with a machine.
examples: I will {print} the tickets at home.
wrong: I print a letter by sending it by email only, with no paper.

words.meaning: To keep a file so you can use it later.
examples: Remember to {save} your work.
wrong: I save my work by deleting it.

words.meaning: To let other people use or see something that is yours.
examples: I will {share} the photos with you.
wrong: I share my sandwich by eating it all alone.
